Hathor. The goddess of love, beauty, fertility, and joy, and also a protective cosmic force. She was depicted as a cow-headed goddess or as a woman with a solar disk between cow horns, representing fertility and celestial abundance. Associated with love, music, dance, and intoxication, Hathor embodied all forms of ecstasy and celebration that brought joy to mortals and gods alike. Sometimes portrayed as Ra's eye, she served as a fierce form that defended him against threats. The Eye of Ra could embody her wrathful aspect when cosmic order was endangered. She was a protective mother figure, depicted nursing or protecting the pharaoh, ensuring his divine legitimacy and divine nurture. As a goddess of fertility and sexuality, women invoked her for pregnancy and childbirth, and she was celebrated in erotic contexts throughout Egyptian life. She was also associated with foreign lands and trade, making her a protector of Egyptian merchants and travelers abroad. Hathor was depicted as gentle and generous in her loving aspects, but fierce and destructive when defending Ra or the cosmic order. Her major cult center was at Dendera, where her temple became a center for healing, fertility rites, and celebration. She shared a connection with Amon through their mutual associations with fertility and generative cosmic forces. Though both Hathor and Isis were protective mothers, Hathor had broader associations with love, beauty, music, and celebration.
